name: infra_ray_train
title: Ray Train TorchTrainer: the per-worker loop is a value handed to a framework, never called in this file
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: an orchestrator MLView has no table for, wrapped around a loop it does
note: The point of this program is the call graph: `train_loop_per_worker` has no call site in the workspace - it is passed to TorchTrainer as a keyword argument and Ray calls it in another process. MLView still finds the loop, the loss, the optimizer and the eval pass, reports nothing, and declares an honest `unresolved_callee` gap for the eight ray.* calls it cannot read. That is the right answer and this program is the guard on it. Two smaller observations: `workspace.frameworks` reports `pandas` on a file with no pandas import, because `scaler.fit_transform(x_train).astype("float32")` at line 76 resolves the ndarray method to `pandas.DataFrame.astype` (see INFRA-R2-06); and `deliver` is absent although ray.train.report(...) at line 133 and CheckpointConfig at line 148 are the checkpoint channel here, which is the TF/ray half of the round-1 INFRA-04 family (see INFRA-R2-07).
stagesObserved: config, data, preprocess, model, objective, train and eval present; `deliver` reported absent. local and ip are byte-identical on this program.

forbidden.why: train_test_split runs at line 72 and the scaler is fitted at line 76 on x_train, which already carries TRAIN_SPLIT; x_val only reaches scaler.transform at line 77
x_val reaches scaler.transform (line 77), never fit or fit_transform
there is no cross-validation call in this program
the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 103; ray.train.torch.prepare_data_loader at line 107 swaps in a DistributedSampler and keeps the shuffling
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False at line 105
no DataLoader here passes num_workers, and Ray - not this module - owns worker process creation
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is the first statement of the training step at line 122
optimizer.step() is called at line 127, after loss.backward() at line 125
the order is zero_grad (122) -> forward (123) -> loss (124) -> backward (125) -> clip (126) -> step (127)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
OneCycleLR is a per-BATCH scheduler and scheduler.step() is called inside the batch loop at line 128, which is its correct cadence
clip_grad_norm_ at line 126 sits between the backward at 125 and the step at 127
evaluate() calls model.eval() at line 88 and model.train() at line 95 on the way out
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator at line 85
the accuracy comparison at line 92 is on model(features).argmax(dim=1), not on raw logits
RiskNet.forward returns self.head(self.body(x)) - raw logits - and there is no softmax anywhere
ray.train.torch.prepare_model at line 111 moves the module and prepare_data_loader at lines 107-108 moves every batch; there is no device literal in this file to be inconsistent about
there is no .cuda() and no 'cuda' literal; use_gpu=True on the ScalingConfig is Ray's own placement flag

seed_everything is called at line 100 inside the worker loop and at line 137 in main(); it calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed, torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed_all, and train_test_split passes random_state=seed
train_test_split passes random_state=seed at line 73
RiskNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 53
the body is an nn.Sequential and the head is assigned directly; there is no plain list or dict of submodules
there is no torch.save and no torch.load anywhere; Ray's CheckpointConfig owns persistence
